assertions.description: The Iterator global constructor from iterator helpers (the object the method hangs off) is exposed.
Iterator.prototype.join is a function (Chrome 153 developer trial: chrome://flags/#enable-javascript-harmony).
join() with no argument uses a comma separator, matching Array.prototype.join.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof Iterator === 'undefined' || typeof Iterator.prototype.join !== 'function') return false; function* g(){ yield 1; yield 2; yield 3; } return g().join() === '1,2,3'; })()

assertions.description: undefined and null elements stringify to empty strings, matching Array.prototype.join semantics.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof Iterator === 'undefined' || typeof Iterator.prototype.join !== 'function') return false; function* g(){ yield undefined; yield null; } return g().join('-') === '-'; })()

assertions.description: Joining an empty iterator returns the empty string.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof Iterator === 'undefined' || typeof Iterator.prototype.join !== 'function') return false; function* g(){} return g().join('×') === ''; })()

assertions.description: join composes with the shipped iterator helpers and consumes lazily: joining take(3) of an instrumented infinite generator pulls a bounded number of values and yields the right string.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof Iterator === 'undefined' || typeof Iterator.prototype.join !== 'function') return false; let pulled = 0; function* inf(){ for (let i = 1; ; i++) { pulled++; yield i; } } const s = inf().take(3).join('+'); return s === '1+2+3' && pulled === 3; })()

assertions.description: Non-string elements go through ToString exactly like Array.prototype.join (nested array case).
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof Iterator === 'undefined' || typeof Iterator.prototype.join !== 'function') return false; function* g(){ yield [1,2]; yield 'x'; } return g().join(';') === [[1,2],'x'].join(';'); })()
